newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ciller promises action against crime and drugs.
newsitem.headline: Ciller promises action against crime and drugs.

text.p: Turkey's deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller, faced with opposition calls for her resignation, pledged on Saturday to act against drug dealing and organised crime.
"I give special importance to the fight against drugs. Death merchants who poison our youths will be incapacitated," Ciller said in a message to newly-appointed Interior Minister Meral Aksener.
"Mafia rumours shake the confidence in the legislation and the state. The source of these rumours would be dried up regardless of their origin," she added.

Aksener, a woman MP from Ciller's True Path Party (DYP), took office on Friday after former minister Mehmet Agar resigned following a scandal pointing to links between security officials and a gangster wanted for political killings and drug dealing.

Ciller had denied that Agar resigned as a direct result of the scandal that has unfolded since a police chief, a fugitive mobster and a former beauty queen died in the same car in a traffic accident last weekend.
Agar said he had resigned to enable a thorough investigation of the accident.
The main-opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) urged Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Ciller on Saturday to resign.
"Agar's resignation is a right decision, but not sufficient. The prime minister and deputy prime minister should also resign," ANAP deputy chairman Salih Yildirim said.

Sedat Bucak, an MP from Ciller's party and a southeastern tribal chief who heads thousands of village guards in a fight against Kurdish separatist guerrillas, was also in the car and injured seriously in the accident.
Turkish newspapers criticised Ciller for the appointment of Aksener whom they say has no experience in security affairs.
"New minister is from the family," headlined mass-circulating Milliyet.
It said the appointment of Aksener, a teacher of history by profession, was a sign that Ciller -- also Turkey's foreign minister -- seeks to run the interior ministry directly herself.
